Murali Maddula | Metabolic Health Advocate on Instagram: "White Rice + Rajma Curry… does adding protein and fiber automatically mean a smaller glucose spike? 👀 Rajma brings fiber and plant protein to the plate, but it brings carbohydrates too! Based on portion estimates, this meal of 200g cooked Sona Masuri rice + 200g rajma curry contained approximately 90g of total carbohydrates. Fiber and protein can influence digestion and glucose absorption, but they don’t cancel out carbohydrates. Food pairing matters and so does portion size. My CGM recorded a 44-point rise, with a relatively quick climb, a rounded top and a sharp drop. The graph alone cannot tell us how much the fiber or protein helped. Next experiment: the same meal with two teaspoons of pure cow ghee + two boiled eggs. Will the rise be smaller, will the peak happen later, or will the response stay similar? We’ll examine the full curve! Watch till the end and share with a rajma-chawal lover! Experiment & Disclaimer: I am not diabetic, and this personal experiment is for educational purposes only, not medical advice. @glucosegoddess #21
Jessie Inchauspé on Instagram: "Small, everyday changes can be a powerful tool for type 2 diabetes. Here are some of my favourite glucose hacks: 👉 Start your meal with veggies - a green salad, roasted asparagus, anything that has plenty of fiber. Fiber forms a protective mesh in your gut, which slows down digestion and helps glucose enter your bloodstream more gradually. 👉 Move your muscles after you eat - walking for 10 minutes, dancing, doing a few squats… pick your favourite. Your muscles use glucose for fuel, helping reduce the spike. 👉 Try apple cider vinegar before a carb-heavy meal - 1 tbsp diluted in a large glass of water. The acetic acid in vinegar can slow the rate at which glucose enters your bloodstream. But there’s more!! Comment HACKS and I’ll send you my full list of 10 glucose hacks. ❤️"

@foundmyfitness #38
Dr. Rhonda Patrick on Instagram: "Eating blueberries improves vascular function. One cup per day is effective, but half a cup does not not produce the same benefit. Adults with metabolic syndrome that ate one cup rather than only a half-cup or matched placebo improved flow-mediated dilation (FMD) by about 1.5 percentage points in a six-month randomized trial. FMD measures how effectively an artery widens when blood flow increases, essentially a “stress test” for the endothelium. It’s relevant because studies have shown it is a strong predictor of future cardiovascular disease events. The one-cup dose is consistent with other studies showing cardiovascular, metabolic, and brain-health benefits of blueberries. My latest solo episode explores the wide-ranging health benefits of blueberries. Watch or listen now on YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Podcasts."

Cleo Abram on Instagram: "What really happened to the ozone layer? Remember when it had a huge hole? Now it’s shrinking! Here’s what happened: The ozone layer is high in the atmosphere and shields us from radiation. But in the early 80’s scientists noticed the ozone above the south pole was depleting…. fast. Scientists suspected that chemicals in everyday products were rising into the atmosphere and destroying ozone molecules. So scientist Susan Solomon led an expedition to the south pole and proved that the chemicals, called chlorofluorocarbons, were to blame. Her work became the basis for the UN Montreal Protocol, which banned chlorofluorocarbons in 1987. Since then, emissions have dropped dramatically and the latest data from NASA satellites shows that the ozone layer is recovering! @ral.livezy #109
Ralston D'Souza on Instagram: "Crispy Soya Chilli Recipe by @humbiharsehain Ingredients: Boil 60g raw soya chunks in hot water with 1 tsp salt until softened. Squeeze out all the excess water. Transfer the soya chunks to a bowl and add: 1 tsp black pepper powder 1 tsp red chilli powder 1 tsp ginger garlic paste Mix everything really well. Now add 2 tbsp cornstarch and toss until the soya chunks are evenly coated. Pop them into an air fryer at 200°C for 10 minutes, flipping halfway through. Once they’re lightly golden and crispy, take them out and set aside. Now let’s make the sauce! In a bowl, add: 1 tbsp Schezwan sauce 2 tbsp soy sauce ¼ cup green chilli sauce ½ cup tomato ketchup 1 tsp vinegar ½ tsp salt ½ tsp cornstarch 50ml water Mix everything really well until combined. Now heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan on medium heat. Add 8 finely chopped garlic cloves and 10g ginger. Sauté until fragrant. Then add 1 finely chopped onion and sauté until lightly golden. Now toss in: 1 chopped green chilli ½ diced onion ½ diced bell pepper Turn up the heat and sauté until the veggies lose their raw bite but still have a nice crunch. Now add the crispy soya chunks and pour in the prepared sauce. Toss everything together and cook on high heat for 2 minutes until the sauce coats the soya chunks beautifully. Finish with ½ handful of fresh coriander, give it one final toss, and it’s ready to serve! Nutrition (Serves 2) Calories per serving – 331 kcal Protein – 18g Carbs – 47g Fats – 9g Fiber – 4g"

The rules aren’t as simple as “bring two bottles.” India’s baggage rules set a duty-free allowance, but you can carry more in checked baggage if you’re willing to pay the applicable customs duty. You also need to declare quantities above the permitted duty-free limit. And there’s one rule many travellers forget: state laws can apply after you land. States such as Gujarat and Bihar have additional restrictions on alcohol possession. So before you pack that extra bottle, check both the customs rules and the alcohol laws of the state you’re travelling to. @idris_workout2 #135
Idris | Online Fitness Coach on Instagram: "✅ The Perfect Assisted Pull Ups (Assisted Pull-Up Machine) 🎯 Target Muscles: Back muscles and biceps 🏋🏽 Equipment: Assisted pull-up machine 📊 Difficulty Level: Beginner to intermediate Step 1 — Starting Position 1. Select an appropriate weight on the machine. The more weight you select, the more assistance the machine provides. 2. Kneel on the knee pad or place your feet on the platform, depending on the machine’s design. 3. Grip the bar with a full grip, wrapping your thumbs around it, with your palms facing forward (pronated grip). 4. Brace your core, maintain a neutral spine, and keep your head aligned with your body. 5. Keep your shoulder blades down and back (scapular depression and retraction) while performing the movement. Step 2 — Pulling Up 1. Exhale as you bend your elbows and pull your body toward the bar. 2. Drive your elbows down and toward your sides. 3. Avoid swinging your body or using momentum. Perform the movement with control. Step 3 — Returning to the Starting Position 1. Continue pulling until your chin reaches the level of the bar or slightly above it. 2. Pause briefly, then inhale as you slowly lower yourself back to the starting position until your elbows are almost fully extended. 3. Maintain proper shoulder positioning, wrist alignment, and body control throughout the entire range of motion. 4. Repeat the movement. Step 4 — Exercise Variations 1. Reduce the weight selected on the machine to decrease assistance and increase the difficulty. 2. Use different grip variations, such as wide, shoulder-width, or neutral grip, to change the emphasis on the back and arm muscles. 3. Maintain proper technique throughout the full range of motion to help minimize unnecessary stress on the shoulder joint. 📚 Source: American Council on Exercise (ACE) #assistedpullups #pullups #gymtok #gymfam #nycfitness"

Where in most households in India, a device more important than an air purifier is actual a kitchen chimney that catches a lot of fumes at source... Air purifiers have only just crossed about 5% of urban households... In Delhi, fewer than 20% of higher-income households owned one. And chimneys? Many Indian households still see them as a luxury, not a necessity... While air purifiers in India are roughly a USD 600 Mn category, growing at 13-14% p.a... kitchen hoods as a category is just about USD 200 Mn... So there are three action points: 1/ If you cook daily, get a chimney with real suction and clean the filters. 2/ Add a purifier for what escapes, not as a substitute. 3/ If you’re a founder: the gap is in kitchen-specific purification, ductless options for small flats, and filter subscriptions. Dr. Pal Manickam (MD, MPH, AB (Gastro), DipIBLM) on Instagram: "Have you tried Ragi Ambali? This traditional fermented ragi drink deserves a place in your routine! Ingredients • Ragi flour (finger millet): ¼ cup • Water (for slurry): ⅓ cup • Water (for cooking): ¾ cup • Water (for fermentation): 1½ to 2 cups • Curd (yogurt) or buttermilk: ½ cup (whisked) • Salt: To taste • Chili-ginger paste: 1 tbsp • Fresh coriander leaves: ½ cup (chopped) • Onions: Finely chopped (optional) Step-by-Step Recipe 1. Make the Ragi Slurry • Mix ¼ cup of ragi flour with ⅓ cup of water in a bowl until smooth and free of lumps. 2. Cook the Porridge • Heat ¾ cup of water in a pan until it comes to a boil. • Reduce the heat to low and slowly pour in the ragi slurry while stirring continuously. • Cook on low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens into a glossy paste. • Turn off the heat and let the mixture cool completely. 3. Ferment Overnight • Once cooled, shape the ragi mixture into small balls. • Place the balls into a clay pot (or a glass/steel container) filled with water. • Cover the pot with a clean cloth or lid and let it ferment overnight (about 8 to 12 hours) in a warm spot. 4. Mix and Season • The next morning, thoroughly mash the fermented ragi balls right into the water until completely dissolved. • Add ½ cup of whisked curd or buttermilk to the mixture and churn well. • Stir in the salt, chili-ginger paste, chopped coriander leaves, and chopped onions (if using). 5. Serve • Serve chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing, gut-friendly morning or midday drink"

Seeing the detail and effort that went into recreating such an important part of our heritage was truly remarkable. 3. 📍 AE Block, Salt Lake This was a 360-degree immersive experience that made me look at everyday objects differently. Such that it is banned in Europe, and Canada allows no more than 0.01% formaldehyde in such heat treated straightening products... This year, India also banned the import of a Keratin Hair Straightening product that had close to 10% formaldehyde... 2/ Now because there has been a lot of education around formaldehyde... the formaldehyde-free products that have come use Glyoxyclic Acid... which has now been found to cause acute kidney injury... Israel has banned it and France has advised against it... So even if you pay a premium for formaldehyde free treatment, that in itself is harmful... NRI Shaala by Aspora on Instagram: "You Moved Back to India. But You’re Not an Ordinary Resident Yet. After 15 years abroad, you finally move back to India. You cross the 182-day threshold and become a resident, but that doesn’t necessarily make you an Ordinarily Resident. That’s where RNOR (Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident) comes in. Imagine you return on October 5. You’re under 182 days for that financial year, so you remain a non-resident. But the following year, you’re in India for the entire financial year and become a resident. Because you were non-resident for at least 9 of the previous 10 years, you can qualify as RNOR. And that distinction matters because RNOR status can significantly affect what India taxes. If you’re planning to move back after years abroad, understanding these three categories before you return can make a huge difference. #NRIShaala #NRI #RNOR #TaxResidency #IndianTax ReturningToIndia NRIIndia TaxPlanning"

Dr. Rhonda Patrick on Instagram: "Drinking water can be a meaningful source of microplastics and associated chemicals, including BPA and PFAS, and reverse osmosis is one of the most effective ways to reduce them. I recently installed a reverse osmosis filter on my kitchen faucet. I wanted filtered water not only for drinking and cooking, but also for washing produce. Soil and water contamination can expose fruits and vegetables to persistent chemicals, so this gives me another practical way to reduce daily exposure. People often ask whether reverse-osmosis water needs to be remineralized. It does not. You can obtain those minerals through your diet. But remineralization may improve the taste if purified water seems flat or unfamiliar. The most important thing is to look for an NSF certification that covers the contaminants you care about and review the system’s performance data. That should tell you what the filter has actually been tested to reduce, and by how much. It can also help address concerns about plastic particles being introduced by the filtration system itself. No filter eliminates every exposure. But because we use water every day, reverse osmosis can be a useful way to reduce the total burden from microplastics and persistent chemicals."

IDP’s FastLane is an interesting example of what happens when you rethink the process instead of simply trying to speed it up. By matching student profiles with participating universities’ entry requirements upfront, FastLane can provide eligible students with an in-principle offer within minutes. IDP says over 1.2 lakh students have received instant offers, and average offer times at participating UK Russell Group universities have fallen from around 30 days to five. The business lesson? Sometimes the biggest innovation isn’t doing something faster. It’s questioning why it takes so long in the first place. Of course, an in-principle offer isn’t the same as final admission. But knowing where you stand earlier can make planning your applications a whole lot easier. #Ad [IDP India, IDP FastLane, IDP study abroad, instant university offers, study abroad 2026, UK university admissions, Russell Group universities, masters abroad, university application process, study abroad counselling, overseas education India, study in UK, study abroad applications, university admission offers, education technology, business case study]"

Add: 1 bay leaf 2 cardamom pods 4 cloves black peppercorns Sauté for about 30 seconds until fragrant, then add: 200ml tomato purée ½ tsp turmeric powder 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder 1 tsp coriander powder 1 tsp salt Mix everything really well and cook until the tomato purée thickens and the raw smell disappears. Let’s understand the steps first. 1/ Supply Chain Financing: BYD took an average of 275 days to pay its suppliers in 2023... whereas most global carmakers usually pay in under 90. In effect, suppliers were funding BYD’s growth... and in a way lending it money interest free to keep operations going... One research firm, GMT, argued that BYD’s true net debt was closer to 323 billion yuan, not the 27.7 billion yuan it reported as of mid-2024... 2/ Chinese Subsidies: Apart from financing from suppliers... BYD received at least $3.7 billion in direct subsidies, with aid jumping from €220 million in 2020 to €2.1 billion just two years later... On top of that, China exempted EVs from purchase tax for years, which made every BYD cheaper for buyers as it was a strategy for the country to flood the market with EVs... 3/ With those two big sources of financing, came the third thing, which literally broke it... Zero-mileage Sales... A number of Chinese companies were selling EVs to corporations in the thousands... and these new EVs would then just sit on parking lots collecting dust, not running... And some time later, the companies would put them on the market for sale as second hand cars with no mileage on them... The industry practice was to register a car right after production so it counts as sold, then label it “used” for export... @hubermanlab #231
Andrew Huberman, Ph.D. on Instagram: "ENTRAINMENT GOVERNS YOUR ENERGY & FOCUS • Entrainment is one of the most powerful aspects of our biology. Our circadian rhythm is created within us, but numerous studies show that our health is best when it is entrained to the rising and setting of the sun. That’s not to say you have to wake up at sunrise, but people who try to live nocturnally definitely suffer health consequences and people who match their sleep rhythm even somewhat to the rising and setting of the sun (one form of entrainment), derive many health benefits. Entrainment works on shorter time scales too. Exercise at roughly the same time for a few days and you’ll notice your energy will increases a few minutes before that typical workout time. Study or do some reading or some other form of work or learning at roughly the same time or times per day, and you’ll notice that your mental sharpness will start to increase in anticipation of those times. To be clear, some of this is psychological, but a lot of it is physiological. The neuromodulators, hormones and neurotransmitters that regulate alertness and focus are readily susceptible to entrainment. And entrainment is a concept that we can leverage. Not to make us rigid, but understanding it can help you make better sense of why you are more energetic and mentally sharp at particular times of day, and it can give you flexibility over what those times are. Each of us has to follow a different schedule, but for me, because I like to get up early and get the dog walked and exercise early and then drop into work, I’ve noticed that my peak focus occurs first from 10 AM to 2PM, and then again between about 3 PM and 7 PM. And again 9-midnight. (But I prefer to sleep by 10:30-11). That’s just me. Figure out your schedule. You can leverage entrainment to get the most out of your workouts and work, etc. Two or three days on a regular schedule usually does the trick. No need to be overly rigid. Please put any questions you have below and thank you for your interest in science!"

The Anti-Doomscroll Briefing

Neutralizing the 10 Psychological Traps of Social Media

Mainstream short-form video algorithms are intentionally engineered as behavioral casinos—optimizing for time-on-screen rather than signal. Inspired by the educational breakdown in "The Brain Behind Your Phone Addiction. We Caught Him!" (Satvic Movement), Instagram Digest inverts this model:

1. Infinite Scrolling

Solved Replaced with a finite weekly batch and an explicit "You're All Caught Up! 🎉" milestone screen.

2. The Red Colour Trap

Solved Zero red badge counts or alarm dots. Replaced with quiet-luxury OLED slate tones and an optional 1-tap Grayscale Detox mode.

3. Gamified Friendship

Solved Completely severed social graph. Zero streaks, zero interaction scores, zero social obligation loops.

4. The Anticipation Trap

Solved Deterministic static compilation. Zero slot-machine pull-to-refresh roulette or delayed typing indicators.

5. Filtered Reality

Solved Whitelist ingestion targeting high-signal creators in science, tech, crafts, and finance, with lifestyle filters.

6. Customised Feed

Solved Replaces black-box recommendation neural nets with an open, fair-share algorithm capping creators at 4 reels.

7. Artificial Urgency

Solved Completely ignores 24h disappearing stories and live broadcasts. Asynchronous weekly briefing on your schedule.

8. Likes and Followers Count

Solved Completely strips like counts, view tallies, follower numbers, and public comment threads from the screen.

9. Simplicity (Hypnotic Trance)

Solved Introduces active decision friction: manual-advance option, 3-second breathers, and active session time-boxing.

10. The Buzz

Solved Zero real-time push notifications or vibration pings. 100% quiet, passive, on-demand pull model.
